choices.text: Graph A, because its line is steeper
Graph B, because its axis goes up to 200

questions.explanation: The trap is: A steeper line always means a bigger increase. Slope depends on the axis scale: two graphs can have the same rise but look different. Both sales rose by 20, so the increase is the same even though the drawings look different.
questions.misconception: A steeper line always means a bigger increase.
questions.prompt: Two line graphs show sales rising. Graph A looks much steeper than graph B, but graph A has an axis of 0 to 50 and graph B has an axis of 0 to 200, and both sales rose by 20. Which graph had the bigger increase?

questions.explanation: Scene s1: 3 of the 12 pupils chose bananas, and 3 out of 12 is 1/4 of the whole class.
questions.prompt: In the pie chart of 12 pupils, 6 chose apples, 3 chose bananas and 3 chose grapes. What fraction of the class chose bananas?

questions.answer: Sales dipped in March; 50 plants were sold in April.
questions.explanation: Scene s2: the line dips down to 30 in March, then climbs to 50 in April.
questions.prompt: A line graph shows plants sold: Jan 20, Feb 35, Mar 30, Apr 50. In which month did sales dip, and how many plants were sold in April?

questions.explanation: Scene s3: read the two bar heights, 13 and 8, then subtract: 13 - 8 = 5.
questions.prompt: In a survey of 24 children, 13 chose soccer and 8 chose badminton. How many more chose soccer than badminton? Show the working.

questions.explanation: Scene s1: 6 out of 12 is half the class, so the apple wedge is 1/2 of the pie.
questions.prompt: What fraction of the pie chart is taken by apples, if 6 of the 12 pupils chose apples?
